saints.name: St. Vincent of Lérins
saints.title: Monk
saints.shortBlurb: The monk of Lérins who gave the Church its enduring test of authentic tradition…
biography: Vincent was a monk of the island monastery of Lérins off the coast of Gaul in the first half of the fifth century. Under the pen-name Peregrinus he wrote the Commonitorium, a short treatise on how to distinguish true Catholic doctrine from heresy.

There he set down his famous rule: that we hold to what has been believed “everywhere, always, and by all” (quod ubique, quod semper, quod ab omnibus). This “Vincentian Canon” has guided theologians ever since. He died about 445.
saints.knownFor: The rule for discerning authentic Catholic teaching — held everywhere, always, by all.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 24 May
